name: References
description: Cite as you write, from your reference manager: Zotero (live, or its library exported with Better BibTeX), JabRef, Mendeley, EndNote or any BibTeX, CSL JSON or RIS file, and references of your own as notes. Pandoc's citations ([@ahrens2017, p. 33]) show in the style you pick (APA, Chicago, MLA, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver or any CSL style), with the note's references in the right sidebar and at the end of an exported PDF.

findBibliographies.label: Find bibliography files
findBibliographies.description: every .bib and .ris file in the vault, and CSL JSON or YAML files named like a library (My Library.json, references.csl.yaml)

bibliographies.label: Bibliography files
bibliographies.description: more files to cite from; the vault's BibTeX (.bib), CSL JSON (.json), CSL YAML (.yaml) or RIS (.ris) files, beside those found on their own, and a note's bibliography: adds its own

zoteroLocal.label: Zotero on this computer
zoteroLocal.description: the Zotero app's library, live; on the server's computer, Zotero 7 or later, with Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero on in its Settings, Advanced

style.label: Citation style
style.description: a style the app has or a .csl file in the vault; apa, chicago-author-date, modern-language-association, harvard-cite-them-right, ieee, nlm-citation-sequence, and a note's csl: says its own

locale.label: Language
locale.description: a code like en-US; a locales-<code>.xml file from the CSL project in the vault adds one, and a note's lang: says its own

inDocument.label: References in document
inDocument.description: under a note's text, as in an exported PDF

folder.label: Literature notes folder
folder.description: where a new one goes; default: where the others are, else Literature

template.label: Literature note template
template.description: a note to make them from; {{citekey}}, {{title}}, {{authors}}, {{year}}, {{bibliography}}, {{doi}}, {{url}}, {{zotero}} and {{annotations}} filled in
